matchstick.title: Chain equality via operator conversion
matchstick.principle: If the right side contains two identical numerals separated by a plus or minus, you can move a single stick to turn that operator into an equals sign. When the left side numeral can be made identical to the repeated numeral (or already is), the result is a chain equality of three identical terms, which is always true.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation has the form A = B ± B and B is a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '=' while leaving the left side unchanged, producing A = B = B where A ≠ B, which makes the equality false.

matchstick.title: Single‑stick numeral reduction
matchstick.principle: A numeral that differs from another by exactly one stick (e.g., XII vs XI) can be altered by moving that stick. Making the two numerals identical often enables a chain‑equality transformation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When one numeral is one stick away from matching another numeral in the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from a numeral and discarding it, leaving the source numeral incomplete and invalid.

matchstick.title: Preserve stick orientation
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their original orientation; a diagonal stick cannot be used as a vertical stick and vice‑versa. Rotating a stick changes its type and violates the puzzle rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you relocate a stick, keep its angle (vertical, horizontal, or diagonal) unchanged.
matchstick.example: Using a diagonal stick from an X to form a vertical I, which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: No addition or removal of sticks
matchstick.principle: Exactly one existing stick must be moved; you cannot create a new stick or discard a stick. The total stick count stays constant.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any transformation, verify that you are only relocating a stick, not adding or deleting one.
matchstick.example: Adding an extra horizontal stick to the equality sign to turn it into '≠'.

matchstick.title: Maintain valid characters
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, every numeral and operator must still be a legal Roman numeral or one of the allowed operators (+, –, =). Any shape that does not correspond to a standard symbol is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each proposed move, check that no character has become an illegal shape.
matchstick.example: Removing a stick from X, leaving a single diagonal line that is not a Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic correctness
matchstick.principle: The transformed equation must be mathematically true. Compute the numeric values of both sides to ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After you have a candidate equation, evaluate its numeric value before finalising the answer.

matchstick.title: Operator swap via stick exchange
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred from one operator to another, changing both symbols while preserving orientation. For example, moving a horizontal from ‘=’ to ‘‑’ turns ‘=’ into ‘‑’ and ‘‑’ into ‘=’.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains multiple operators and a stick can be moved between them to produce valid operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from '+' to '=', leaving '+' as '-' and '=' as an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: Removing a stick from an X or a V leaves a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral. Such moves must be avoided.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider taking a stick from an X or V, ensure the remaining shape is still a valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Taking one diagonal from an X, resulting in an isolated diagonal character.

matchstick.title: Cross‑numeral stick transfer
matchstick.principle: A stick can be moved from one numeral to another, potentially changing both values, as long as each resulting numeral remains valid. This is useful when one numeral is one stick away from the target value.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral can be altered by gaining or losing a single stick and another numeral can spare that stick without becoming invalid.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from 'XII' to the minus sign, but leaving 'XII' as an invalid shape.

matchstick.title: Track stick orientation counts
matchstick.principle: The numbers of vertical, horizontal, and diagonal sticks must be unchanged after the move. Counting each orientation before and after helps catch accidental additions or deletions.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a move, tally sticks of each orientation to ensure the totals match the original configuration.
matchstick.example: Creating an extra horizontal stick in the result, implying a stick was added rather than moved.

matchstick.description: Rotating sticks (treating a diagonal as vertical or vice‑versa)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes sticks are interchangeable and forgets that orientation is fixed in the puzzle.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, keep its original angle; never use a diagonal stick to form a vertical I or an I to form a diagonal part of X/V.

matchstick.description: Adding or removing sticks instead of moving exactly one
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model interprets the task as allowing extra sticks or discarding sticks, overlooking the relocation constraint.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count sticks before and after; ensure the total number of sticks stays the same and that every move is a relocation.

matchstick.description: Creating invalid numerals after a move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the operator change and neglects the validity of the resulting characters.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character still matches a standard Roman numeral or allowed operator.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after forming a syntactically plausible equation, ignoring the numeric truth of the equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides of the candidate equation and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Changing operators to disallowed symbols (e.g., turning ‘=’ into ‘≠’)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any visual modification of an operator as permissible, missing the limited operator set.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Restrict operator changes to the three allowed symbols (+, –, =) and never introduce other symbols.
